title: Utility Line Locator
description:
**Job Overview**

As a Utility Line Locator, you’ll help protect underground infrastructure by identifying and marking utility lines before excavation begins. You’ll use utility locating devices, review site information, and communicate findings clearly to clients and construction crews. The role combines field service with outdoor work across varied job sites. Your impact: Accurate utility marking helps crews plan safer excavation and reduces the risk of damage to underground utilities.

**Responsibilities**

* Locate and mark underground utilities, including cabling, using appropriate locating devices and methods.
* Review construction plans, site plans, and schematics to understand site conditions and identify potential conflicts.
* Document findings and explain markings, limitations, and site conditions to clients and construction teams.
* Follow safety protocols while working near active utilities, construction activity, and changing outdoor conditions.
* Operate a company vehicle and maintain locating equipment and field records.

**Skills**

* Utility locating, utility marking, and experience with utility locating devices are central to this role.
* Service technician, field service, land surveying, or construction site experience is helpful, as is experience in the energy and utilities sector.
* Ability to interpret site plans, construction plans, and schematics; familiarity with ground-penetrating radar or vacuum excavation for utility detection is a plus.
* Demonstrated safety protocol adherence, clear client communication, and comfort with outdoor work are important.
* A valid driver’s license and safe company vehicle operation are required.

title: Manufacturing Process Engineer, Electrified Energy Storage
description:
**Manufacturing Process Engineer, Electrified Energy Storage**
==============================================================

**Start with the mission**
--------------------------

Battery manufacturing rewards discipline and punishes improvisation. Tiny process slips compound into major quality escapes; early instability drains margins. Your mission is to engineer safe, efficient, and repeatable assembly processes so scale is predictable and customers can rely on every module and pack we ship.

**Your impact**
---------------

* **Engineer end-to-end assembly:** Architect and document complete manufacturing flows for battery modules and packs, defining sequence and work content to meet quality, takt, and safety/ergonomics.
* **Codify the work:** Build visual, precise standard work and instructions tied to drawings/BOMs, current revisions, and approved changes—and train the team.
* **Equip the line:** Specify, install, commission, and sustain tools, fixtures, inspection/test equipment, and material handling aids; validate equipment readiness and settings.
* **Stabilize ramps:** Support initial launch, volume ramp, and new variant introductions; act fast on process issues, bottlenecks, or downtime with corrective actions.
* **Control variation:** Define in-process checks, error-proofing (poka-yoke), and capability/control plans; drive root cause analysis and CAPA with Quality.
* **Bridge design to build:** Evaluate manufacturability impacts from engineering changes, update processes/instructions, and support pilot builds for smooth NPI transitions.
* **Relentlessly improve:** Deliver gains in yield, cycle time, labor efficiency, and scrap/rework by applying lean methods and improving flow.
* **Protect people:** Ensure EHS compliance and safe work practices; identify and mitigate ergonomic and safety risks across assembly and material handling.
* **Make it measurable:** Maintain accurate process definitions, equipment settings, and change histories; report process me
